item.title: Geidai Worldbuilding
item.description: Tokyo University of the Arts (Geidai) · July 7–10, 2026 Instructor: Peter Brinson, Professor of Practice, University of Southern California Through lectures, exercises, and workshops, students explore worldbuilding as a foundation for game design and development.

item.title: Assignment C - From Maze to Labyrinth
item.description: Continue with your project. From Assignment B - Bounded World, keep your closed world’s boundary as a primary element in the experience.

item.title: Week 5.2 - Worldbuilding 1, Finite Worlds
item.description: Let us study worldbuilding in parallel to storytelling in games. The Bounded Worlds Framework couples nicely with The Situated Player Roles.

item.title: Week 5.2 - Labyrinths
item.description: Labyrinths What a Labyrinth Is Labyrinths are expressive mazes. That is, they are vehicles for a story, or they are metaphors themselves.

item.title: Project 3 — The Dreamer
item.description: Situated Player Role Reading: The Dreamer — World as Enigma Learning Goals: Color theory and lighting; interactive storytelling; arc of experience; game engine literacy; camera principles; materials and textures; sound design; ideation, brainstorming, and prototyping; self-direction; critique.
